q: Is Bihać good for a family holiday with kids?
a: Yes, Bihać is good for a family holiday because it is quiet, nature is right on the doorstep and distances are short. Children love walks along the Una, the waterfalls of Una National Park, Plitvice about 35 km away and family rafting on the calmer stretches. For families we recommend houses on the Una with a garden, where children have room to play.

q: What can I do with kids in Bihać?
a: With children in Bihać you can walk along the Una and feed the ducks, visit the Captain's Tower (Kapetanova kula) and look out over the town from the top, visit Japodski otoci and Štrbački buk, and swim at designated spots in summer. Older children enjoy family rafting, kayaking and cycling. Ostrožac, with its park of stone sculptures, is also interesting for children.

q: What is the minimum age for rafting on the Una?
a: The minimum age depends on the section and the water level: for the demanding section from Štrbački buk, organisers usually do not recommend it for children under 12, while on the calmer Kostela – Grmuša section they usually take children from about 6. The final decision is always made by the organiser based on the state of the river. We organise rafting with Una Olympic Rafting from Grmuša/Salihovac, so ask us about a family trip.

q: Is rafting on the Una safe for children?
a: Rafting with a licensed organiser on a calmer section and at normal water levels is considered suitable for children, with a compulsory life jacket, helmet and skipper. In spring the water level is higher and the river faster, so the summer months are better for families. Children must follow the skipper's instructions, and a shorter, calmer route is usually recommended for younger children.

q: Does my child need to be able to swim to go rafting?
a: It is preferable for a child to be able to swim and not be afraid of the water, although all participants wear a life jacket. For more demanding sections, organisers recommend good swimmers. Before booking, tell the organiser your child's age and swimming experience so they can suggest a suitable route.

q: Where can children swim safely in the Una?
a: Children are safest swimming at shallow, calm spots near the bank, at designated bathing areas in Bihać and by riverside restaurants and camps, always supervised by an adult. The Una is cold even in summer, and in some places it has a strong current and sudden drops. Avoid swimming near waterfalls and rapids and never let children into the water alone.

q: How cold is the Una for children to swim in?
a: The Una is a relatively cold river even in summer, so swimming is refreshing, but children get cold quickly. It is best to swim during the warmest part of the day, for shorter periods, and to have a towel and dry clothes ready. Shallow spots near the bank are a little warmer than the main current.

q: Are there playgrounds in Bihać?
a: Yes, there are several children's playgrounds in Bihać, in town parks and residential areas, some of them by the river. Some restaurants and hotels in the area also have play areas, which is handy while the parents have lunch. If you stay in a house with a garden on the Una, the children have room to play right outside the door.

q: What is the Japodska kućica na drvetu (treehouse) near Bihać?
a: Japodska kućica na drvetu (the Japod treehouse) is one of our properties on the Una, accommodation built up in the treetops that children and families especially love. The combination of staying in a tree and being close to the river makes it appealing for an adventurous family holiday. Check availability, number of beds and price by sending an enquiry on apartmanibihac.com or via WhatsApp/Viber +387 61 591 320.

q: Is the treehouse safe for young children?
a: The treehouse has stairs and a raised terrace, so young children need constant supervision by their parents. For families with babies or toddlers, a ground-floor house with a fenced garden is often more practical. Before booking, ask us for details about access and railings, and we will suggest the most suitable property.

q: Do you have houses with a garden for families near Bihać?
a: Yes, most of our houses and holiday cottages on the Una in Lohovo, Pritoka and Grmuša have a garden, and many also have a barbecue and space to play. They include Green River, Vila Enio, Villa Džane, Villa Mekić and Vikend kuća Bašić. A whole house costs from 25 to 100 € per night, depending on the property and season, and a whole apartment from 25 € (50 KM), which is what a single room for one person usually costs in Bihać.

q: Do your apartments have a cot for a baby?
a: At Apartman M. Mahala (Midžić Mahala) a cot is available on request. At our other properties a cot and high chair are not standard, so mention them in your enquiry when you send your dates and number of guests, and the owner will confirm whether they can be provided. Send your enquiry on apartmanibihac.com or via WhatsApp/Viber +387 61 591 320; you will get a reply within 12 hours.

q: Do children pay for accommodation?
a: With us, the price is for the whole property, not per person, so there is no separate charge per child; you pay for a property that suits the size of your group. Prices are from 25 to 100 € per night for the whole property. It is important to state the exact number of adults and children in your enquiry so the owner can suggest a property with enough beds.

q: How far is Plitvice from Bihać, and is it doable with kids?
a: The Plitvice Lakes are about 35 km from Bihać, roughly 35 to 40 minutes' drive via the Izačić border crossing. For children, the shorter routes around the lower lakes are best, combined with the boat and the panoramic train. Buy tickets in advance on the official Plitvice Lakes National Park website and set off early to avoid the crowds.

q: Is Štrbački buk suitable for children?
a: Yes, Štrbački buk is suitable for families: well-maintained paths and wooden footbridges lead from the car park to the viewpoints, and the walk is short. Young children must stay with their parents, as the paths are close to the water. The last part of the road to the waterfall is gravel, so allow a little more driving time.

q: Is Japodski otoci a good place for kids?
a: Yes, Japodski otoci in Račić near Bihać is good for children: small islands connected by footbridges, sculptures of the Japodes, plenty of space to run around and a restaurant by the river. It is about 15 km from the centre of Bihać. Keep an eye on children near the water, as the Una flows fast between the islands.

q: Are there child-friendly restaurants in Bihać?
a: Yes, many restaurants on the Una and in the surrounding area have gardens where children can play, and some have playgrounds. Breaded chicken, chips, pancakes and pizza are common on menus, and portions are generous, so they are easy to share. Not all restaurants have high chairs, so ask when you book.

q: What can picky eaters eat in Bihać?
a: Fussy children will easily find something in Bihać: pizza, pancakes, breaded chicken, ćevapi (grilled minced-meat rolls) in flatbread, chips and ice cream. Bakeries sell burek (meat-filled filo pie), cheese pies and rolls. If you are staying in an apartment or house, the kitchen lets you cook familiar meals yourself.

q: Where is the hospital in Bihać?
a: The main hospital in Bihać is the Cantonal Hospital 'Dr. Irfan Ljubijankić' (JZU Kantonalna bolnica „Dr. Irfan Ljubijankić”), which has a paediatric ward and a paediatric surgery department. In an emergency, call an ambulance on 124. For minor problems, first go to the health centre (dom zdravlja) or a pharmacy. Save the number in your phone before heading out on day trips.

q: Can tourists see a paediatrician in Bihać?
a: Yes, paediatric care is available at the Bihać Health Centre (Dom zdravlja Bihać) and at the Cantonal Hospital 'Dr. Irfan Ljubijankić', and there are also several private paediatric practices in town. Foreign visitors usually pay for the consultation unless they have international health insurance that covers it. In an emergency, call 124.

q: Do children need travel health insurance in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: Yes, travel health insurance is recommended for all family members, including children, when staying in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The European Health Insurance Card is not automatically valid here, and the rules depend on your country's agreements with Bosnia and Herzegovina. Buy insurance before your trip and keep the confirmation.

q: Are there pharmacies in Bihać, and are any open at night?
a: There are many pharmacies in Bihać, mostly in the centre, and usually at least one is on duty at night and at weekends. The duty rota is posted on pharmacy doors and locally. It is still a good idea to bring basic children's medicines, such as fever syrup, from home. Your host can also tell you which pharmacy is on duty.

q: What is the drive to Bihać like with children?
a: Bihać is easy to reach by car from Croatia via the Izačić or Velika Kladuša border crossings, and from Zagreb the drive takes about two and a half to three hours. Child car seats are compulsory as required by law. In summer and at weekends, expect waiting times at the border, so bring water and something to keep the children entertained.

q: Do children need a passport to enter Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: Yes, every child needs their own valid travel document: a passport, or for citizens of some countries an ID card. If a child is travelling with only one parent or with other adults, it is advisable to carry a certified letter of consent from the other parent. Check the rules for your nationality before travelling.

q: What is the best accommodation in Bihać for a family with young children?
a: For families with young children, the most practical options are a ground-floor house on the Una with a fenced garden or a spacious apartment in the centre near shops and pharmacies. Quiet villages such as Lohovo are ideal for children's sleep routines. With us, a whole apartment starts from 25 € (50 KM) per night, the same price as a single room for one person in Bihać.

q: Is it dangerous for children to stay in a holiday house by the river?
a: The river is a big advantage of the houses on the Una, but it calls for caution: gardens are not always fenced off from the water, and the Una can be deep and fast. Young children must not be left alone outside. If a fence matters to you, mention it in your enquiry and we will suggest a suitable property.

q: Are there summer events for children in Bihać?
a: In summer there is plenty for children in Bihać: the Bihaćko ljeto (Bihać Summer) festival includes children's performances, and during the Una Regatta the town is full of events. On top of that there is swimming, playgrounds, ice cream by the Una and short trips into nature. The children's programme is published by the Bihać Cultural Centre (Kulturni centar Bihać).

q: Are there farms with animals for children near Bihać?
a: Yes, some rural farms and eco-villages around Bihać and near the entrance to Una National Park have farm animals, playgrounds and space for children. Children love visiting them, and parents can try home-cooked food at the same time. What is on offer and opening hours depend on the season, so ask us for a current recommendation.

q: Is Bihać pushchair-friendly?
a: In the centre of Bihać and along the riverside promenade a pushchair can be used without major problems, as the ground is flat. At sights such as Sokolac and Ostrožac there are steps and uneven paths, so a baby carrier is more practical. At Štrbački buk the paths have wooden footbridges and steps, so a carrier is a better choice there too.

q: Is Ostrožac Castle interesting for kids?
a: Yes, children usually find Ostrožac fascinating: an old fortress with ramparts, towers and a courtyard full of stone sculptures in which they can look for shapes and figures. It is about 20 km from Bihać, roughly 25 minutes' drive. Keep an eye on children on the ramparts and stairs.

q: When is the best time of year for a family holiday in Bihać?
a: For families, the best time is late June, July and August, when it is warm enough to swim and rafting is on calmer water. Late May and September are quieter and pleasant for walks and day trips, but the Una is then too cold for swimming. In spring the water level is high, so rafting is not suitable for young children.

q: Can children go kayaking or paddleboarding on the Una?
a: Yes, older children can try kayaking, canoeing or stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) on calm stretches of the Una, wearing a life jacket and supervised by an experienced guide or parent. These activities are offered near Račić, Kostela and other places along the river, mainly in summer. Check the minimum age and conditions with the organiser.

q: Is the Captain's Tower in Bihać interesting for children?
a: The Captain's Tower (Kapetanova kula) is interesting for older children because of its narrow staircase, the old prison and the view from the top over Bihać and the Una. The exhibition on the Japodes and the region's ancient history can be told as a story about an ancient people living by the river. The visit is short, so it fits easily into a walk around town.

q: How many days should we spend in Bihać with children?
a: With children we recommend three to five days, as they need a slower pace and time to play. Your plan could include a day on the river, a day at Štrbački buk, a day at Plitvice and a rest day in the garden of a house on the Una. Send your accommodation enquiry on apartmanibihac.com with the number of children and their ages.

q: Are there supermarkets near the holiday houses on the Una?
a: The biggest choice of supermarkets is in Bihać, which is a few minutes from Pritoka, about 15 minutes from Lohovo and a somewhat longer drive from Grmuša. Larger villages have small shops with basic groceries. It is best to buy nappies, baby food and medicines in town before heading to the house.

q: Is Bihać safe for families?
a: Yes, Bihać is a quiet town and families generally feel safe there, and the centre is busy even in the evening. The main need for caution relates to nature: the river, waterfalls and traffic on local roads. With the usual care, Bihać is well suited to a family holiday.

q: Can we bring our dog on a family holiday in Bihać?
a: Pet rules differ from property to property, so for holiday houses you must mention your pet in your enquiry. The owner will confirm whether the pet is allowed and whether there are any extra conditions. Of our properties, Apartman M. Mahala (Midžić Mahala) in Bihać accepts dogs and also has a cot available on request. Keep your dog supervised near the river.

q: Are there swimming pools for kids in Bihać?
a: There are pools at some hotels and sports facilities in Bihać, and some are open to non-guests for a fee. In summer, though, most families swim in the Una. Check opening hours and terms of use directly with the venue. In summer they are often busy, so arrive early.

q: How do I book family accommodation in Bihać?
a: To book family accommodation, send an enquiry on apartmanibihac.com with your dates, the number of adults and children and any requests such as a cot or a garden. At Apartman M. Mahala (Midžić Mahala) a cot is available on request; for other properties, please ask in your enquiry. The owner confirms availability within 12 hours, and you pay in cash on arrival.

q: Is there a scenic train ride along the Una that kids would enjoy?
a: A tourist train ride through the Una valley is occasionally organised in summer, for example as part of the Una Regatta, and children usually love it for the views of the river, the tunnels and the bridges. These rides are not a regular service, so check dates and conditions with the organiser. Follow announcements from the City of Bihać and Una National Park at npuna.com.
